cases.original_question_en: Which spec-to-spec section-reference pairs are most frequent? (cross-spec coupling)
cases.error_origin: released original Core query, benchmark gold, or legacy answer/scoring contract, as identified below
cases.released_original_query: MATCH (a:Section)-[:BELONGS_TO_SPEC]->(sa:Spec), (a)-[:REFERENCES_SECTION]->(b:Section)-[:BELONGS_TO_SPEC]->(sb:Spec) WHERE sa.specNumber <> sb.specNumber RETURN sa.specNumber AS fromSpec, sb.specNumber AS toSpec, count(*) AS refCount ORDER BY refCount DESC LIMIT 10

released_answer_contract.contract_disposition_label: question text is the only thing that would have to change

cases.observed_problem: The English asks most frequent with no k. The original LIMIT10 returns the ranked positive pair pool rather than only maximum-frequency pairs.
cases.repair: Count distinct directed reference relationships per spec-number pair, compute the maximum over the complete eligible pair pool, and return every maximum tie.
cases.repaired_reference_query:
MATCH (a:Section)-[ref:REFERENCES_SECTION]->(b:Section),
(a)-[:BELONGS_TO_SPEC]->(sa:Spec),
(b)-[:BELONGS_TO_SPEC]->(sb:Spec)
WHERE sa.specNumber <> sb.specNumber
WITH sa.specNumber AS fromSpec, sb.specNumber AS toSpec,
count(DISTINCT ref) AS referenceCount
WITH collect({fromSpec:fromSpec,toSpec:toSpec,referenceCount:referenceCount}) AS pairs,
max(referenceCount) AS maximumFrequency
UNWIND pairs AS pair
WITH pair, maximumFrequency WHERE pair.referenceCount = maximumFrequency
RETURN pair.fromSpec AS fromSpec, pair.toSpec AS toSpec

cardinality_policy.extent: all recorded directed cross-spec specNumber pairs tied at the highest frequency of distinct section-reference edges; no arbitrary k

cases.original_question_en: Return the most-referenced sections within spec 38.413 (identifying key sections).
cases.error_origin: released original Core query, benchmark gold, or legacy answer/scoring contract, as identified below
cases.released_original_query: MATCH (s1:Section)-[:BELONGS_TO_SPEC]->(sp:Spec {specNumber: '38.413'}), (s1)-[:REFERENCES_SECTION]->(s2:Section) RETURN s2.sectionId, count(*) AS refs ORDER BY refs DESC, s2.sectionId LIMIT 10

released_answer_contract.contract_disposition_label: question text is the only thing that would have to change

cases.observed_problem: The original query constrains source s1 to38.413 and returns s2 without that target-membership clause. It also imposes an unasked top10. An actual out-of-spec returned row is not inferred from this code defect.
cases.repair: Place38.413 membership on the requested target Section, include zero-reference targets, count all recorded incoming Section references, and return all maximum ties.
cases.repaired_reference_query:
MATCH (target:Section)-[:BELONGS_TO_SPEC]->(:Spec {specNumber:'38.413'})
WITH DISTINCT target
OPTIONAL MATCH (:Section)-[ref:REFERENCES_SECTION]->(target)
WITH target, count(DISTINCT ref) AS referenceCount
WITH collect({sectionId:coalesce(target.sectionId,target.iri), referenceCount:referenceCount}) AS candidates, max(referenceCount) AS maximum
UNWIND candidates AS candidate
WITH candidate, maximum WHERE candidate.referenceCount=maximum
RETURN DISTINCT candidate.sectionId AS sectionId

cardinality_policy.extent: Most with no explicit k naturally means maximum incoming frequency and every equal maximum. Capture all eligible target counts, including zero; collect-plus-max returns all maxima instead of inventing k10 or a count threshold. A separate full-pool witness is required before admission.

cases.original_question_en: Return the top 10 agenda items by resolution count (busiest agenda areas).
cases.error_origin: released original Core query, benchmark gold, or legacy answer/scoring contract, as identified below
cases.released_original_query: MATCH (r:Resolution)-[:RESOLUTION_BELONGS_TO]->(ai:AgendaItem) RETURN ai.agendaNumber, count(r) AS cnt ORDER BY cnt DESC, ai.agendaNumber LIMIT 10
cases.observed_problem: The original query groups by reusable agendaNumber and truncates with LIMIT 10; its scalar-set reference cannot represent the complete entity rank pool and boundary alternatives. In the corrected full source pool, the top 10 boundary has five tied agenda identities for two remaining slots.
cases.repair: Group by the actual AgendaItem entity and capture the complete 3,582-item pool including zeros. Require exactly 10 eligible identities, all eight higher-ranked identities, and any two of the five boundary ties; do not require an unasked count field or lexical tie-break.
cases.repaired_reference_query:
MATCH (ai:AgendaItem)
OPTIONAL MATCH (r:Resolution)-[:RESOLUTION_BELONGS_TO]->(ai)
WITH ai, count(DISTINCT r) AS resolutionCount
RETURN coalesce(ai.id, ai.iri) AS agendaId, resolutionCount
ORDER BY resolutionCount DESC
